correctness.rationale: The exact half-line normalization and all claims check analytically. After dropping the scalar energy and rescaling time by Ω/2, the boundary resolvent entry is −w^s/(1−iηw), where z=−w−w⁻¹ and |w|<1 for Im z>0; this follows from the free decaying solution and the first-row boundary equation. Laplace–Plancherel gives η/π times its real-energy squared integral. The boundary limit is justified by |1−iηw|≥1 and a uniform integrable squared tail from |w|≤1/(|z|−1). On the band put w=e^{ik}; off the band put w=±q on the two tails. The energy Jacobians give exactly F+G_s in RESULT.md. Reciprocal subtraction gives the positive claimed integrand; successive distances multiply it by q². Differentiation gives P_s′(1)>0 and strict increase on (0,1]; at both ends P_s tends to zero for s≥2, so maxima exist strictly above 1. The η-uniform bound G_s≤1/[2πs(s−1)] and strict isolated maximum of F localize all maxima. F″(1)=−2/(3π) and compact-local G_s″=O(s⁻²) give eventual strict concavity. The beta moment at η=1 gives P_s′(1)=1/(2πs³)+O(s⁻⁴); the stationary equation and quadratic expansion give respectively 3/(4s³) and 3/(16πs⁶) with the claimed errors. At s=1 the substitution t=ηq instead gives the exceptional strong-loss limit 1. The supporting script was inspected, not run; its finite-chain comparison is not an exact tail certificate, and no such certificate is needed for the analytical proof. No uniqueness for small s is inferred.
